decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 4.25%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Eric S. Rosengren.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 4-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 4-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: Incoming information suggests that economic growth is slowing, reflecting the intensification of the housing correction and some softening in business and consumer spending.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “However, the pace of economic expansion will likely slow in the near term, partly reflecting the intensification of the housing correction.”

changes.quote: Moreover, strains in financial markets have increased in recent weeks.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Economic growth was solid in the third quarter, and strains in financial markets have eased somewhat on balance.”

changes.quote: Today’s action, combined with the policy actions taken earlier, should help promote moderate growth over time.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Today’s action, combined with the policy action taken in September, should help forestall some of the adverse effects on the broader economy that might otherwis…”

changes.quote: Readings on core inflation have improved modestly this year, but elevated energy and commodity prices, among other factors, may put upward pressure on inflation.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Readings on core inflation have improved modestly this year, but recent increases in energy and commodity prices, among other factors, may put renewed upward pr…”

changes.quote: Recent developments, including the deterioration in financial market conditions, have increased the uncertainty surrounding the outlook for economic growth and inflation.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 4-1/4 percent.
Incoming information suggests that economic growth is slowing, reflecting the intensification of the housing correction and some softening in business and consumer spending.
Recent developments, including the deterioration in financial market conditions, have increased the uncertainty surrounding the outlook for economic growth and inflation.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.59% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.98% and moved -17 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.1% would fall by about $32.81 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.7%, and employers added an average of 92k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.4% over the past year (November 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.3%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -23 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 31%, cut 69%, hike 0%.
